title: Credential namespace, TTLs, and per-scope key governance
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our current API key surface mixes long-lived credentials, user-scoped tokens, and service keys with inconsistent naming and no enforced TTLs. This causes operational confusion, audit noise, and security exposure for Dedicated/Private customers. Objective: introduce a credential namespace + naming convention, default and max TTLs, per-scope (fine-grained) keys, and an automated rotation orchestration that integrates with audit logging and SSO guardrails.

Scope:
- Define immutable parts of a key identifier (namespace, type, scope, owner) and a human-friendly display name pattern.
- Enforce default TTLs for interactive (dashboard) keys and caps for programmatic service keys.
- Add per-scope key issuance (e.g., embeddings:read, runtime:invoke:modelX) and tie scopes to RBAC v2 roles.
- Build rotation orchestration: scheduled rotation jobs, one-click force-rotate in Console, and silent rotation for dedicated host agents.
- Emit structured audit logs for creation/rotation/revocation with old/new key fingerprints.
- UX: Admin console flows for creating scoped keys, previewing TTLs, and a ledger view for active credentials.

Non-goals: automatic re-encryption of customer-managed keys (KMS work tracked separately), migration of all legacy keys in the first phase (we will provide a migration path), and changing how tokens are validated at runtime (no runtime verification changes planned here).

Design decisions & rationale:
- Namespacing: prefix format <org>-<env>-<type>-<owner>-<shortid> to make keys discoverable across projects and to allow automated scavenging for stale keys. Avoid embedding sensitive data in names.
- TTL policy: interactive_console keys default to 7 days, service_keys default to 90 days with max 365 days. This balances developer ergonomics vs risk for programmatic access.
- Per-scope keys: scopes are declarative strings mapped to RBAC v2 roles. We will limit number of scopes per key to 10 to reduce complexity in audit entries.
- Rotation model: offer both scheduled (recommended) and manual rotation. Rotation should be atomic from the caller's perspective: new key must be issued and propagated before old key retired. For Dedicated customers we will coordinate with capacity agents to avoid in-flight KV cache disruption.
- Audit logging: store key events with key_fingerprint (SHA256 truncated), issuer (SSO user ID), action, effective_ttl, scopes, and optional linked_pr/issue for context. Logs must be queryable by key_fingerprint and org.

Acceptance criteria: (see acceptance_criteria field)

Rollout plan: phased:
1) Implement backend schema for namespaced keys, TTL enforcement, scope mapping. Feature-flagged.
2) Expose admin APIs + CLI for key issuance/rotation. Start internal dogfood and run migration tools for infra services.
3) Add Console UI for scoped key creation and ledger. Run closed beta with 3 customers.
4) Expand to full rollout with migration assistance and a deprecation schedule for legacy keys older than 18 months.

Metrics to monitor: number of active keys by TTL bucket, rotation rate, failed rotations, audit-log volume per org, and customer support tickets referencing lost/compromised keys.
acceptance_criteria: Backend stores namespaced identifier and computes key_fingerprint for every credential
API enforces default TTLs and rejects create requests exceeding configured max_ttl
Console can create per-scope keys and shows effective scopes and TTL before creation
Rotation endpoint supports atomic rollover and returns old/new fingerprints for audit
Audit logs contain structured entries searchable by fingerprint and org id
Feature flag exists to enable/disable new issuance behavior per environment
tasks: Schema: add credential_table fields: namespace, type, owner_display, fingerprint, scopes, expires_at
API: POST /v1/credentials with scope validation and TTL enforcement
Console: scoped key creation UI and ledger row actions (rotate/revoke)
Rotation service: orchestrator for scheduled/manual rotation with retry/backoff
Audit: wire credential lifecycle events into our structured audit pipeline
Docs: PRD + developer docs and migration playbook for legacy keys
E2E tests: issuance -> rotation -> revocation flows and audit verification
